Columbus County deeds go to Suite B at 125 Washington Street, Whiteville. Letters go to PO Box 1086, Whiteville, 28472. Weekday hours run 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., except on county holidays.

Filing stops a quarter hour before the doors close: recording intake ends at 4:45 p.m. daily. Marriage license applications stop even sooner, at 4:30 p.m.

Sellers reach this office last. The deed that moves title, along with the lender's deed of trust, is filed here, usually by your attorney or the title company. Mostly you need to keep the cutoff in mind when reading a closing calendar.

An ordinary deed is $26.00 for its first fifteen pages and $4.00 for each further page. The county's fee notice cites G.S. 161-10, a schedule that applies the same way in every North Carolina county.

Fees posted by the Columbus County Register of Deeds
DocumentFee
Deed of trust$64.00 covers 35 pages, then $4.00 a page
Other instruments (deeds, easements, most agreements)$26.00 covers 15 pages, then $4.00 a page
Plat$21.00 per page
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trustFree of charge
  • A release of a paid-off mortgage is recorded at no cost to the seller. Certified copies are $5.00 on page one and $2.00 per page following, and a UCC filing is $38.00 for 2 pages.
  • Plain copies, whether made at the counter or ordered by mail, are 25 cents a page. Deeds can also be viewed free in the online system.
  • A notary oath taken at the office carries a $10 fee, payable by cash or local check.

Excise tax is the seller's cost, collected by the register ahead of filing. G.S. 105-228.30 sets it at one dollar for every $500 of price or value, rounding a partial $500 up, and the county FAQ restates that as $2 per thousand dollars of purchase price. The county general fund takes half; the rest goes to the state revenue department.

The tax scales with price and prints as a separate settlement line. Staff cannot quote it for a sale unless they have the deed, so ask your closing attorney for the number before signing day.

A name change on title needs a new deed at the usual $26.00 rate. The office recommends an attorney to draft it and cautions that excise tax can apply.

Everything except plats can be recorded electronically, and approved vendors appear on the e-recording page of the register's website. A closing package filed that way can make the 4:45 p.m. cutoff with nobody driving to Whiteville.

The online index works by name, so each search begins with a person or company rather than a house number, and staff cannot say who owns a given street address. Use the county tax office, home to the land records and mapping staff, when you need ownership by address.

  • Look up the owner's name and open the recorded deed.
  • Match the deed's legal description to your tax bill.
  • Scan the deed of trust section for a mortgage that never got a satisfaction.
  • Mechanics liens and judgments are a Clerk of Court question, and the register's FAQ sends you to the courthouse.

When two claims compete for one piece of land, the recording date settles it. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed, option, lease over three years or right of first refusal shields its holder from lien creditors and paying buyers only once registered in the land's county, and whoever registers first ranks higher. A signed deed alone does not finish a sale, because until the register stamps a recording time on it, a later claim could still move ahead.

Seller financing follows the same logic. Chapter 47H covers a home for one to four families sold on five or more payments while the seller keeps title. Recording falls to the seller, who has five business days to file the contract or a memorandum, and the buyer has three business days to cancel. Read the full chapter before choosing this route.

A parcel near active farming picks up a warning in the land records under Session Law 2018-113. The triggers are a qualifying poultry, swine or dairy farm, or a voluntary agricultural district, within one-half mile, or any other qualifying farm within 600 feet.

Your buyer's title search may flag the parcel. Nobody can sue over a researcher's failure to report the notice, and brokers and appraisers are not liable for omitting it. It informs; it does not restrict the sale. About 54 people live per square mile on the county's 938.12 square miles of land, which makes farm neighbors common. Buyers will ask about it, so have an answer ready.

If you file the deed without a closing attorney, check the basics before you drive to Whiteville. Confirm the page count so you can bring the exact fee, since payment is due at filing. Have the seller's excise tax figure in hand, because staff will not calculate it without the deed. Plan to arrive well before 4:45 p.m., and ask an attorney to draft the document, because register staff do not draft or correct deeds.

After recording, you can view the deed in the online system at no charge or order a certified copy at the counter.

Columbus is rural, with about 50,487 residents and 23,724 housing units. Owner-occupants live in 71.1% of homes, and the median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 was $146,000. Just 55 building permits were issued in 2025, so almost every deed moves an older house. Measure your price expectations against that median, and have your closing attorney pull the county records you need before listing.

Bills are due September 1. Pay the tax office by mail, phone, drop box or counter, or online at columbus.webtaxpay.com; the mailing box is PO Box 1468, Whiteville.

The bill carries no penalty until early January. A 2% charge then applies January 6 through the end of that month, and starting February 1 three-fourths of one percent accrues for every month or part of a month (G.S. 105-360). Because the real property tax lien attaches on the listing date (G.S. 105-285, G.S. 105-355), your bill follows the parcel into the sale.

Before closing, ask the tax office for a payoff figure and hand it to whoever prepares the settlement statement. Seniors and disabled owners claim homestead relief on Form AV-9 through the assessor; ask there for current forms. If back taxes or repairs make an ordinary sale hard, a cash sale is another route; see our North Carolina page.

faqs.q: Who files the deed after a Columbus County sale?
faqs.a: The register's office in Whiteville. Your closing attorney or title office normally submits the package, at the counter or through an e-recording vendor, before the 4:45 p.m. intake cutoff.

faqs.q: What does the register charge for a deed here?
faqs.a: A flat $26.00 covers fifteen pages, and each added page is $4.00. A deed of trust runs $64.00 for 35 pages.

faqs.q: Who owes the deed excise tax on a Columbus County sale?
faqs.a: The seller. The register collects at the counter before filing, at one dollar per $500 of price or value, which the county FAQ words as $2 per thousand dollars.

faqs.q: Can the Register of Deeds look up who owns a certain address?
faqs.a: No. The retrieval system is name based, so a search needs a person or company name. Use the county tax office for address-based parcel records.

faqs.q: Where do I ask about liens and judgments on a Columbus County property?
faqs.a: Ask the Clerk of Court at the courthouse. Also check recorded deeds of trust for any unreleased mortgage.
